description: Per-institution statutory financial statements (individual licensed banks' IFRS reports) were not located as a browsable NBU index; only aggregated/grouped data was found.
All NBU endpoints in this slice are unverified for automated liveness because the host returned 403 to the tooling used.

Payments-market statistical series from the NBU (card transaction volumes, POS/ATM terminal counts, cashless payment share) were not pinned to specific dataset URLs in this slice; only the payments registers and oversight pages were captured.
English mirrors were confirmed to exist for the main NBU sections (/en/statistic, /en/stability/report, /en/news/all) but were not systematically enumerated per source.
No archival strategy identified for NBU PDFs whose URLs carry mutable ?v= cache-busting suffixes.
Sense Bank disclosure tree unmapped (no reporting page, no confirmed IFRS PDF).
Bond-listing-venue disclosure (offering circulars, noteholder notices) for Oschadbank eurobonds/LPNs not located.
IFI counterparty disclosure (EBRD, IFC, World Bank project pages carrying state-bank due-diligence and covenant material) not yet catalogued in this cell.
English-language coverage is thin for Ukrgasbank and Sense Bank — searches surfaced only uk-language reporting pages.
NBU (bank.gov.ua) per-bank supervisory statistics and NSSMC (stockmarket.gov.ua) disclosure portal were not directly probed in this slice.
The actual member-list pages of НАБУ, АУБ and УАФІК were identified but never rendered — only their URLs/navigation were captured.
No association was found covering POS/terminal vendors, processors, ATM operators or cash-in-transit — the payment-infrastructure supply side.
English mirrors exist (aub.org.ua/en, fintechua.org/en, vaks.org.ua/en) but were not compared against the Ukrainian versions.
All rosters found are point-in-time; no archive of past membership was located, so entries/exits cannot be reconstructed retrospectively.
It is unclear whether ЄМА and УАФІК flagship reports are fully public or members-only/form-gated; only a mirrored 2023 fintech catalogue PDF was located as an open copy.

No regional or niche Ukrainian financial outlets (e.g. Ekonomichna Pravda's regional peers, Telegram/YouTube analyst channels run by banking journalists) were scouted; these often break results stories ahead of the mainstream desks.
No archive or backfill route was established for any outlet — pagination limits, sitemap availability and whether historic league tables remain online are unknown.
Interfax-Ukraine and Opendatabot both gate their most structured outputs behind commercial subscriptions/APIs; terms and pricing were not established.

Media rankings in this cell almost all derive from the same upstream NBU statutory reporting, but the exact NBU dataset and its release calendar were not mapped in this cell (it belongs to a regulator cell).
No candidate in this slice was fetched directly; all were identified via search-result evidence, so liveness, paywall depth and robots/ToS specifics remain unconfirmed.
This slice establishes the register/aggregator channels but does not yet produce the actual list of EDRPOU codes for Ukrainian banks and licensed payment institutions.

The cell rationale assumes aggregators preserve documents after issuer sites go offline, but no evidence was gathered on whether any of them retain original PDF filings versus only normalised data fields.
English-language coverage of Ukrainian registers is thin: aggregator English interfaces exist (YouControl /en/) but were not assessed for field parity with the Ukrainian version.
Smaller or niche Ukrainian register aggregators (e.g. ring.org.ua, edrpou.info-type sites) were probed but only edrpou.ubki.ua surfaced with evidence; the long tail of mirror sites is unmapped.

This slice catalogued the archive INFRASTRUCTURE and the regulator-side continuity registers, but did not enumerate individual bank/PSP IR domains and their historical URL patterns (only PUMB was reached concretely).
Non-bank payment sector (PSPs, acquirers, payment-terminal operators, money-transfer systems) has no archival source identified.
Occupied-territory / Crimea-Donbas successor institutions and their disclosure are entirely uncovered.

The 2014-2016 bank-failure wave (which killed roughly half the banking system's institutions) is only indirectly covered via the NBU history page and Minfin aggregator; no verified archived source of those banks' own annual reports was located.
No forward-looking preservation routine is specified — the run treats archives as read-only, but the highest-value action for a wartime market is CREATING captures before loss.
English-language sources dominate the archiving-infrastructure half of this cell; Ukrainian-language querying produced almost nothing on web archiving as such.

International core-banking and card-processing platform vendors (BPC/SmartVista, OpenWay/Way4, Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Diasoft, Colvir, ITTI Digital) have no confirmed Ukrainian-bank engagement mapped.
ATM hardware OEM and ATM-managed-services presence in Ukraine is mapped only through one local service company (Printec Ukraine); no OEM-side Ukrainian customer evidence collected.
Cards/personalisation, cash-handling OEM and ATM-OEM segments were probed largely in English; Ukrainian-language equivalents were not exercised.

Vendor LinkedIn company feeds and conference/exhibition materials (e.g. Ukrainian banking-IT forums, NBU-adjacent industry events, PSM Awards nominee dossiers) were not systematically harvested, though these often carry customer names never posted to the corporate site.
Prozorro was identified but only used through the web UI; the supplier-side view and the open API/bulk exports were not exercised, and buyer EDRPOU codes for the state banks were not enumerated.
Most recovered vendor-bank evidence clusters in 2018-2024; recent (2025-2026) vendor announcements about Ukrainian bank engagements were only lightly sampled, chiefly around open banking.

Only DK 021:2015 66110000-4 was empirically confirmed in searches. Adjacent codes covering payment-terminal supply (POS hardware), processing services, cash-in-transit and card personalisation were not enumerated.

No systematic enumeration of the key buyer entities (Oschadbank, Ukrgasbank, Sense/Ukreximbank as buyers of IT, Ministry of Finance, Treasury, Pension Fund, oblast administrations, municipal transport operators procuring fare acquiring).

Wartime direct-contracting exemptions ('особливості' regime under martial law) allow many contracts to be reported without an open tender; this pass did not map how such banking contracts are disclosed.
Russian-language variants of key terms (эквайринг, расчетно-кассовое обслуживание) were not searched, and some legacy records or aggregator pages may use them.
Municipal-level procurement portals and transport-ticketing operators (e-ticket acquiring) were not explored, despite being a major non-state channel for payment-services awards.

Hungarian- and German-language filings of the parent groups (OTP's BSE/Hungarian filings, RBI's German-language Geschäftsbericht, ProCredit's German annual financial statements) were not searched in this pass.

Other foreign-parent banks in Ukraine were not enumerated systematically (e.g. Citibank Ukraine, ING Ukraine, Deutsche Bank representative presence, Sense Bank post-nationalisation history, TAScombank-type mixed ownership).

Regulated-filing venues for the parents (Vienna Stock Exchange / OeKB ad-hoc disclosure, Budapest Stock Exchange filings, EU ESAP/OAM national storage mechanisms) were not scouted; only issuer-hosted IR pages were.
Structured data artefacts (RBI XLSM results file, OTP iXBRL annual report packs, ESEF/iXBRL filings) were identified only by reference, not located at a stable URL.
All URLs recorded here come from search results or a single fetch; liveness, paywalling and robots/ToS posture were not verified.
Tascombank's own «розкриття інформації»/annual-report page (licence holder for izibank, absorbed Sportbank) was not pinned down; only an ESG subdomain surfaced.

Several other domestic privately owned banks in scope were not reached in this pass: ОКСІ БАНК, Банк «Глобус», Агропросперіс Банк, Банк Восток's peers such as Індустріалбанк, Банк «Український капітал», Полтава-банк, Банк «Портал», Кредитвест, ПІН Банк, Банк Січ successors.
No web-archive strategy was established for banks whose disclosure pages disappear on liquidation (Concord, Sportbank, Sich, Ukrbudinvestbank).

Only Universal Bank's newsroom was identified; the press/newsroom sections of PUMB, A-Bank, Credit Dnipro, Vostok and Alliance were not individually pinned, and neobank founders' Telegram channels (a genuine primary disclosure channel for monobank) were not mapped.
English mirrors were only confirmed for PUMB, MTB Bank, Bank Alliance and Radabank; most private banks appear to disclose in Ukrainian only, and some legacy PDFs are served under /ru/ paths.
No confirmed machine-readable successor to the v1 open-data API for regulated information published after 30/06/2021.
No sector filter in the issuer index means the bank/payments issuer population is not yet enumerated.
Bond prospectus retrieval path for bank issuers is hypothesised, not confirmed.
The disclosure database and all filings are Ukrainian-only; NSSMC's English site covers policy and press but not filing content.
Regulated information may be published via multiple authorised publishers, and only SMIDA has been identified.
Non-bank payments companies are largely outside the issuer disclosure perimeter.
Securities-regulator disclosure channel (NSSMC / SMIDA / stockmarket.gov.ua) not yet mapped for payment-sector bond issuers.

Brand-to-legal-entity resolution is incomplete: only Portmone (EDRPOU 31868613) and Fondy (ТОВ ФК 'ЕЛАЄНС') were resolved. EasyPay, City24 (ФК 'Свіфт Гарант'), IBOX terminals, LeoGaming Pay and iPay.ua lack confirmed EDRPOU codes.
No audit-firm or credit-rating primary source captured. Standard-Rating (Стандарт-Рейтинг) assigned uaAA to NovaPay bonds but its own publication site was not visited.
Almost all substantive disclosure in this cell is Ukrainian-only; English coverage is limited to NBU translations and a NovaPay English profile.
Court and insolvency registries (Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень) not covered, despite litigation and licence-revocation being the main public events in this sector.
Corporate homepages for UPC (upc.ua) and TAS Link (taslink.ua) were inferred from company names and asset paths rather than opened during this pass.

Independent ATM deployers and cash-in/self-service terminal networks beyond UkrCard (e.g. bank-independent ATM operators, IBOX/self-service networks) and the merchant-acquiring PSP layer (Portmone, Fondy, LiqPay, Platon, NovaPay) were not systematically enumerated.
No open-data/API endpoint for NBU card and POS statistics was identified in this pass; only PDFs and HTML pages were found.
English-language NBU payments pages were not sampled; the en mirror may be less bot-defended and easier to collect for headline series.

The full list of per-bank *.fg.gov.ua liquidation subdomain slugs was not enumerated; only five instances (ukrinbank, bnk, concord, ibox, plus the /banki-shcho-likviduyutsya path-based entries) were observed, and the register page is paginated with a JS 'load more' control.
Prozorro.Sale's open-data/API endpoints for the ЦБД1 bankrupt-bank asset stream could not be documented because both relevant pages returned 403 on fetch.

Court-registry coverage of liquidation and resolution disputes was not searched. Shareholders of several resolved banks litigate their market withdrawal for years (the DGF publishes rebuttals on this), and the Єдиний державний реєстр судових рішень would carry those rulings.

Alternative electronic auction platforms besides Prozorro.Sale — notably СЕТАМ and the individual accredited electronic trading platforms named in DGF auction passports (e.g. TOV 'NVP Informatsiyni Tekhnolohii') — were identified only in passing and not scouted as sources.
DGF social/messaging channels (Telegram, Facebook, YouTube) under /novini-ta-media were not enumerated. In Ukraine these are often the fastest publication channel for resolution announcements.
The English-language DGF site was mapped, but it was not established how far behind the Ukrainian site it runs, nor whether annual reports are published in English at all.

Depth of the DGF press-release archive was observed to at least page 30 but the earliest available date and whether the pre-2015 site (old fg.gov.ua URL scheme, e.g. /dlia-vkladnykiv/91-news-uk/...) is still reachable were not established.

The full Section IV list of audit entities entitled to audit public-interest entities (and therefore banks) has not been enumerated; only Big Four plus Grant Thornton, Baker Tilly, BDO and one local firm were identified.

No verified auditor→bank matrix was built for the ~60 licensed Ukrainian banks; only isolated examples (Universal Bank, Bank Globus/Baker Tilly, TASCOMBANK/MTB/Kredobank tender notices) were observed.
Wartime effects on audit timing (deadline extensions, martial-law reporting relief, delayed or unavailable opinions for banks in occupied/resolved status) were not investigated.

Payments-sector coverage (payment institutions, e-money issuers, PSPs under the Law on Payment Services) was not separately probed for audit obligations and auditors — this cell's searches were bank-centric.

The audit committee / ревізійна комісія and corporate-governance disclosures inside bank annual reports (auditor tenure, non-audit fees, rotation dates) were not scouted, though they are the counterpart disclosure to the auditor's own transparency report.

Bilateral European DFIs that co-invest alongside the majors in Ukrainian financial services were identified as co-investors (Proparco, Swedfund, Finnfund, IFU, and by extension KfW/DEG, FMO, BGK) but their own disclosure registers were not scouted.

IFI independent accountability and evaluation arms (IFC CAO, EBRD IPAM and EvD, World Bank Inspection Panel, IEG) were not systematically scouted. These publish the most candid assessments of financial-intermediary lending.
API/bulk-download endpoints were not confirmed for IFC disclosures, EBRD projects, MIGA or EIB. Only the World Bank is known to expose documented public APIs.

IFI annual reports and Ukraine country strategies (EBRD Country Strategy for Ukraine, IFC country strategy, World Bank CPF) were not individually scouted, and their Ukrainian-language summaries — which the cell rationale assumes exist — were not located.

IFI shareholding/equity stakes in Ukrainian banks specifically (as opposed to lending and guarantees) were only partially evidenced — the clearest case found was IFC's Ukrgasbank loan with an option to convert into up to 20 percent equity.
